samples.identification: AES-wrapped PowerShell crypter with protected managed process-hollowing launcher
samples.marker_line: PowerShell crypter: masked loader hollows a native host; retain traits
evidence: Outer script Base64-decodes ciphertext/key/IV, decrypts AES-256 CBC with PKCS7 and constructs then invokes a ScriptBlock over the recovered UTF-8 source. Recovered source is 1131676 bytes.

Start-BeaconCycle polls aspnet_compiler process liveness. It Base64-decodes a blob, XORs each byte by a repeating key and Base64-decodes the resulting text into a 64000-byte managed assembly. It passes aspnet_compiler.exe and a 286208-byte typed native PE array to reflected FILE.WHORE.LAUNCHER.

LAUNCHER RVA 0x207c retries qASnOg2Lc. Its RVA 0x27a0 static constructor constructs an ordered twelve-delegate pipeline. The pipeline creates the host with flags 0x08000004, parses the supplied PE headers, obtains a 179-int i386 context initialized to 0x10002, reads the host image base via context Ebx+8, optionally unmaps it, allocates 0x3000 memory with protection 0x40, writes image headers and sections, rewrites the remote PEB image-base slot, sets context Eax (index 44) to mapped base plus entry RVA, sets the context and resumes the host thread.

Native API names are hidden behind protected strings and typed delegates. ImplMap independently identifies LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress. The argument layouts, header offsets, remote pointers, context stores and twelve-step dispatch order establish the hollowing behavior rather than the assembly/type names.

Embedded native PE begins with a position-independent MZ-header trampoline that computes the PE entry at RVA 0x26c0. Its populated section has an obfuscated dispatcher at RVA 0x1080 and no populated data directories. Final unpacked application identity and downstream behavior are not established.
samples.balance: Encryption and reflective loading can be legitimate. Executing the concealed native image inside a suspended Windows Framework utility, with liveness-based relaunching and no ordinary product context, tips the verdict to malicious. Possession for authorized analysis and runtime success cannot be determined.
samples.changes: No original detection weakened or removed. Existing execution, masked assembly activation and suspended-host injection traits are supported.

samples.identification: Managed XWorm client configured as XWorm V7.1
samples.marker_line: XWorm V7.1: remote tasks and DDoS; add startup and screen exfil
evidence: Settings cctor RVA 0x21e4 provides encrypted config. AlgorithmAES.Decrypt RVA 0x4890 computes MD5 over the embedded mutex seed, copies the digest into a 32-byte AES key at offsets 0 and 15, and decrypts Base64 ciphertext with Rijndael ECB. Reconstruction yields host 31.56.209.61, port 443, group XWorm V7.1, install directory %AppData% and install name windows.exe. The host was not contacted.

Main RVA 0x226c decrypts settings, enforces a mutex, copies current executable bytes to the configured install path, resolves SpecialFolder 7, constructs a .lnk filename, creates WScript.Shell, invokes CreateShortcut, assigns the installed path to TargetPath and calls Save. This is concrete Startup persistence. Plugin RegistryKey.SetValue calls use Software plus ID for cached plugin data, not a Run key.

ClientSocket.BeginConnect RVA 0x25c0 chooses a configured host; ConnectServer RVA 0x2694 establishes a TCP socket, sends a host report and starts BeginReceive. BeginReceive RVA 0x2dbc reconstructs length-framed data and hands completed packets to a worker reaching Messages.Read RVA 0x3300.

Read decrypts the packet, decodes text and splits on the configured delimiter. RunShell extracts argument 1 and passes it directly to VB Interaction.Shell; it is arbitrary command-line execution, not a proven socket/shell-I/O reverse-shell relay. DW writes/launches received content, FM loads a received assembly and invokes its entry, and plugin/savePlugin decompress and reflectively invoke plugins, including registry-cached modules.

The screenshot task copies PrimaryScreen pixels into a Bitmap, scales the image, saves JPEG into a MemoryStream and uses that same stream to produce compressed Base64 in response-array slot 4. It concatenates that array and calls ClientSocket.Send. Send RVA 0x2fe0 AES-encrypts the supplied bytes, adds length framing and calls Socket.BeginSend over the connected control socket.

StartDDos/StopDDos start and abort a worker. TD RVA 0x40f0 starts twenty attack threads per burst with a five-second inter-burst sleep, bounded by the requested duration and connection state. Worker RVA 0x455c connects to the target, sends a POST header promising Content-length 5235, sleeps 2500 ms without a body, and disposes the socket. This corroborates the existing incomplete-POST exhaustion finding.

Antivirus RVA 0x2a88 queries WMI SecurityCenter2 AntiVirusProduct. Existing security-product reconnaissance, plugin tasking, screenshot capture, DDoS and family findings are supported. OfflineGet returns OfflineKeylogger Not Enabled, Spread only compares the current basename with USBNM, and UAC only checks administrator group membership: these names do not prove keylogging, USB replication or elevation.
samples.balance: Task-driven arbitrary execution, screenshot transfer, hidden installation and remote DDoS functionality outweigh a legitimate remote-administration explanation. No consent, controller provenance or deployment context was provided; none was invented.
samples.changes: Add three hostile traits for task-command execution, Startup shortcuts and JPEG screen responses, plus four notable structural/capability observations. Preserve every existing finding.

samples.identification: CrYpToR v2.2 / Universal Polymorphic Device virii demo, active COM infector
samples.marker_line: CrYpToR v2.2: polymorphic COM infection; retain accurate traits
evidence: COM-origin 0x100: entry reaches 0x258 and CALL 0x72d. POP BP/sub 0x25c establishes relocation base; the routine saves the DOS DTA with AH=2f and sets its own DTA with AH=1a.

AH=4e/4f enumerate *.COM. At 0x772 AX=3d02 opens each candidate read/write. AH=3f reads four entry bytes. A fourth-byte marker skips infected hosts; EOF checks reject files under 1000 bytes and over 0xa348. EOF-3 is stored at header+1.

At 0x7ae the program gives its own body to the code-generating engine at 0x14e1 twice with different flags. BIOS INT 1a and PIT port 0x40 feed the rotate/XOR generator at 0x93d. Opcode emission at 0x99c writes paired instruction words. At 0x15ff it saves the output pointer, at 0x165d adjusts it by the paired-buffer displacement and at 0x16b9 calls that exact pointer cell over copied body bytes.

At 0x7d5 AH=40 writes the generated buffer at EOF. AX=4200 seeks to offset zero; AH=40/CX=4 then writes the same E9 displacement-and-marker header. It closes the handle, continues enumeration, restores the DTA and returns to host execution. This is active file modification and replication, not merely a banner or entropy observation.
samples.balance: The demo disclaimer supports a research-origin explanation for possession. The implemented self-appending entry rewrite and generated payload transforms nevertheless establish malicious file-infection behavior. Original deployment and successful execution are unknown.
samples.changes: No trait changes: existing infection, polymorphic concealment and supporting DOS observations are accurate.
